Sources: git diff f42b1a9726 HEAD per file, read at 8479634adc; the ghost-field slot counts were observed with the trunk install (3cec777a08) in native and bytecode; commit messages of cbca48d5d5 (shifts) and ba068ca404 (the #6806 cherry-pick). American spelling.

what.short: The interface of Ast_helper, the smart constructors for Parsetree nodes used by the parser and by ppx rewriters.

vox.short: Adds Typ.refine, an optional ?binder on Typ.arrow, Exp.ghost, Exp.refine, Exp.assume and Exp.let_refine, and the forward hook Typ.map_expression_types.
vox.long: `Typ.varify_constructors` rewrites type constructors into type variables inside a type; a refinement type `{x : t | p}` now contains an expression, whose own type annotations must be rewritten too. `Ast_helper` cannot depend on `Ast_mapper`, so `map_expression_types` is a reference that `Ast_mapper` fills in at initialization.

what.short: The open-recursion iterator over the Parsetree, the read-only counterpart of Ast_mapper.

vox.short: Visits the new nodes: the predicate of Ptyp_refine, the binder of Ptyp_arrow, and the operands of Pexp_ghost, Pexp_refine, Pexp_assume and Pexp_let_refine.

what.short: The open-recursion mapper over the Parsetree, the basis of ppx rewriters.

vox.short: Maps the new Parsetree nodes, and installs the mapper that Ast_helper.Typ.varify_constructors uses on refinement predicates.
vox.long: A ppx that maps types therefore also reaches the type annotations inside refinement predicates, because `Ptyp_refine` recurses into its predicate with `sub.expr`.

notes.title: Filling the forward reference
notes.text: Applies a type rewrite to the outermost types inside an expression by overriding `typ` in `default_mapper`. `Ast_helper.Typ.varify_constructors` calls it on the predicate of a `Ptyp_refine`, so a locally abstract type named in a predicate becomes a type variable like everywhere else.

what.short: Computes the free module names of a Parsetree for ocamldep: the compilation units a source file depends on.

vox.short: Follows refinement predicates, which are expressions inside types, and the operands of ghost_, refine_, assume_ and let refine_.
vox.long: A predicate such as `{x : int | M.valid x}` makes the type depend on `M`, so `add_type` must call `add_expr`, which is defined after it. A forward reference, `add_expr_fwd`, breaks the cycle.

notes.title: Types that contain expressions
notes.text: Set to `add_expr` at the end of the file. Without it, a unit whose only use of `M` is inside a refinement predicate would be missing `M` from its dependencies, and a build would compile it before `M`.

what.short: The interface of Builtin_attributes: attributes the compiler interprets, and tracking of which were used.

vox.short: Exports is_transparent_definition, true for [@def transparent]; the typer, Typedecl and Vox_vc use it to unfold a definition at its full applications.
vox.long: The verifier unfolds a transparent definition at each full application by assuming the refinement of its generated lemma `f_def` at the same arguments (`transparent_definition` in `verification/vox_vc.ml`).

what.short: The interface of language extensions: enabling, disabling and querying -extension flags and their maturity levels.

vox.short: Adds the Refinement_types constructor, and generalizes with_enabled to return the callback's result.
vox.long: `with_enabled` returned `unit`; the typer now uses it to replay generated syntax with fixed extension settings and needs the result.

what.short: The interface of the Parsetree pretty-printer, which prints source code back from an AST.

vox.short: Adds expression_with_type_overrides, which prints an expression while replacing chosen core types (matched physically) with given printers.
vox.long: `Oprint` uses it to print a refinement predicate: `Otyp_refine` keeps the predicate as a Parsetree expression together with a list of the core types inside it and their outcome trees, and those types are printed from the outcome trees by the type printer instead of as source.

what.short: The Lambda intermediate language: terms, primitives, layouts, and helpers used by the Typedtree-to-Lambda translation.

vox.short: Exports placeholder_of_layout, the value an erased ghost expression becomes: dummy_constant for values, zeros for unboxed numbers.
vox.long: Unboxed products get a placeholder per component; vector layouts have none and are a fatal error. `Translcore` uses it for `ghost_ e` and for reads of `@@ ghost` fields.

what.short: The interface of warnings: the type of all warnings with their numbers, and the state that enables and disables them.

vox.short: Adds warnings 222 to 229, the unused_proof_step type for 227 and the trusted_external_reason type for 228, and a refined_unit flag on unused-variable warnings 26 and 27.
long: 222 `Slow_refinement` reports a proof whose solver resource count passes the warning threshold; 223 `Unerased_ghost_body` a function whose result is ghost and whose body is not wrapped in `ghost_`; 224 `Unerased_ghost_call` a call evaluated at run time only to discard its ghost result; 225 `Redundant_ghost` a `ghost_` inside code that is already ghost; 226 `Proof_only_binding` a binding computed at run time but used only in ghost code; 227 `Unused_proof_step` a lemma call, `assume_` or argument refinement whose fact no proof in the function used; 228 `Trusted_external` an external outside the verified library whose refinement or totality the verifier assumes, or a `%identity` cast to total; 229 `Unverified_import` an imported interface whose verification was skipped.
`refined_unit` is set when the unused variable has a refinement of `unit` as its type: the fact holds without the name, and the message says so.

what.short: The extension GADT and its printing and parsing, shared by the compiler and by tools that do not link the parser.

vox.short: Adds Refinement_types : unit t, parsed from the name refinement_types.

what.short: Profiling counters for the typing input, including a count of language extension uses.

vox.short: Adds Refinement_types to the extensions for which no counter exists, so the match stays exhaustive.

what.short: The implementation of Int: externals for the integer primitives, plus a few functions such as abs, equal, min and max.

vox.short: Adds Int.Refined: total division and remainder with a nonzero divisor, and total shifts whose count is proved to be in [0, 63].
long: OCaml leaves `x lsl n`, `lsr` and `asr` unspecified for `n` outside [0, 63], and compiled code disagrees: native code folds `1 lsl 64` to 0, while arm64 computes `1 lsl n` with `n = 64` as 1. The verifier had modeled the out-of-range result as one uninterpreted function, which proved a false equation; the fix (`cbca48d5d5`) gives every shift that verified code performs the obligation `0 <= n && n <= 63`, and made the standard shifts `Stdlib.( lsl )`, `( lsr )`, `( asr )` partial again, like `( / )`.

A total function or a predicate that needs a shift uses `Int.Refined`, whose count is refined to that range; each application is a refinement introduction, so a unit that uses it is verified. The rest of `Int` is unchanged and carries no `@@ total`, so `Int.add` and `Int.shift_left` are partial; `Stdlib.( + )` is total.

notes.title: The refined operators
notes.text: The same primitives as the partial operators (`%divint`, `%lslint`, ...), with a refined second argument and `@@ portable total`. No run-time check is added: the precondition is a proof obligation at each call site. A predicate cannot pass a constant to a refined parameter, so a specification that needs `x lsr 4` names it through a total helper (see `lsr4` in `verification/library/vox_table_wrap.ml`).

what.short: Code shared by the bytecode and native toplevels: phrase parsing hooks, typing of a phrase, printers and directives support.

vox.short: Installs the verifier when the module is initialized and runs Verification.run on each typed phrase before it is compiled.
vox.long: So refinements in toplevel phrases and expect tests are checked the same way as in a compilation unit. `Verification.run` passes `~whole_unit:false`, which disables the per-unit proof cache.

notes.title: Verifying a phrase
from: let typecheck_phrase ppf oldenv oldsig sstr =
notes.text: Runs after `Typecore.force_delayed_checks`, so the phrase is fully typed, and before evaluation, so a refinement that is not proved stops the phrase with an error.

what.short: The toplevel's # directives: #load, #use, #directory, #install_printer, #rectypes and the rest.

vox.short: #rectypes fails when the refinement_types extension is enabled, as Typemod does for -rectypes on a compilation unit.

notes.title: #rectypes
notes.text: The same restriction as `check_refinement_types_options` in `typing/typemod.ml`: equirecursive types and refinement types cannot be combined. `testsuite/tests/typing-refinement-types/rectypes-incompatible*.ml` test all three orders.

what.short: Prints a runtime value from its type, for the toplevel's val x : t = ... output and for the debugger.

vox.short: Prints a refined value through its payload type, and a ghost record field as <ghost>, since it has no slot to read.

notes.title: Refined values
notes.text: The payload alone determines the representation of `{x : t | p}`, so the value is printed as a `t`.

notes.title: Ghost fields
notes.text: A `@@ ghost` field holds no value at run time, so the printer shows a placeholder instead of reading it. (In native code the field has no slot at all; in bytecode the block still has one.)

what.short: The root Dune file: the compiler-libs libraries (ocamlcommon, ocamlfrontend, ocamlbytecomp, ocamloptcomp) with their module lists, and the main executables.

vox.short: ocamlfrontend gains refinement_predicate, verification, vox_type, vox_trust, vox_audit, structural_recursion and recursive_function; ocamlbytecomp and ocamloptcomp depend on vox_verify.
vox.long: `vox_verify` (in `verification/runtime/`) selects `vox_verify.enabled.ml` when `vox_smt_solver`, `vox_vc` and `unix` are available and `vox_verify.disabled.ml` otherwise, which is how the bootstrap compiler is built without a verifier.

notes.title: The bytecode compiler links the verifier
notes.text: The type checker (`typing/verification.ml`) only holds callbacks; linking `vox_verify` and calling `Vox_verify.install` is what makes a compiler verify.

what.short: A Vox-added shell script for the incremental test loop: ./dev init, and ./dev test on test files, directories or --affected BASE.

vox.short: New script that asks ocamltest which artifacts the selected tests need, builds only those with Dune, and runs the tests in parallel against them.
long: `plan_tests` runs `ocamltest -plan-incremental` on each test and `add_requirement` maps each requirement (`expect`, `ocamlc.byte`, `ocamlopt.opt`, `compilerlibs.ocamlbytecomp`, ...) to a Dune target and to an `OCAMLTEST_*` variable that ocamltest reads instead of its installed tools. A test ocamltest cannot plan is refused, with the `make test-one` command to use instead.

`start_test_library` builds the prebuilt test library in the background while tests that do not need it start; `VOX_VERIFY_CACHE` skips re-verifying units with identical inputs; slow proofs are collected into one list at the end instead of appearing as warnings in test output. The compiler host defaults to native. Runs are serialized per worktree with a lock.

notes.title: Requirements to Dune targets
notes.text: Each case adds a Dune target and exports the `OCAMLTEST_*` override that `ocamltest/ocaml_files.ml` reads. With `--compiler-host=bytecode`, the `.opt` actions run the bytecode-hosted compilers, which build faster.

notes.title: Proof cache and slow proofs
notes.text: Solver resource counts differ between platforms, so warning 222 would make test output platform-dependent; the verifier appends slow proofs to `VOX_SLOW_PROOFS` instead, and `dev` lists them after the run.

what.short: The introduction to OxCaml's modes: locality, uniqueness, linearity, portability, contention, statefulness, visibility.

vox.short: Adds a section on totality (total < partial) and inductive pattern matching: why total code may only destructure nonrecursive or [@@inductive] types.
long: It lists what a total closure may not do (call captured partial functions, recurse, loop, raise, match non-exhaustively, read or write mutable state, allocate identity-bearing values), shows the Landin knot that motivates the pattern rule, and covers aliases, recursive modules, functors over `[@@inductive]` signatures, phantom occurrences and type parameters. The rule on mutable state concerns the built-in reads and writes: a total function may still write storage it owns uniquely, through the verified library's total externals.

It says that neither an alias nor a module boundary may hide a cycle. It does not describe the rule for hidden types (GADT existentials, abstract and open types, unpacked modules) that the totality check applies since `09dfd7e2fa`. Ghostliness is not documented in these pages.

what.short: The reference for modes: every axis, its modes, modalities and mode crossing.

vox.short: Adds that data values, including mutable data, cross from partial to total; reading or writing mutable data is partial on its own account.

what.short: The syntax of modes and modalities and the table of implied modalities.

vox.short: Adds the totality axis (total | partial) to the grammar, partial to the legacy modes, and total implies stateless and portable to the implication table.

what.short: The introduction to kinds: layouts, mode-crossing bounds and nullability.

vox.short: The kind of int now lists total among its crossings, and the text says all modal axes instead of eight.

what.short: The syntax of kinds and the definitions of the built-in kind abbreviations.

vox.short: Adds total to the crossings of everything, immediate64, immutable_data, sync_data, mutable_data and their or_null variants.

what.short: The shared engine of the expect-test tools: runs each phrase, captures its output, and rewrites [%%expect] blocks, with separate Principal outputs.

vox.short: Cherry-picks the upstream fix #6806: a single [%%expect] block is split into default and Principal outputs when they differ, and joined when equal.
vox.long: Before the fix, a run with `-principal` overwrote a single expect block with the principal output, so the other run then failed. The same commit makes trailing code after the last block trigger the principal run, and brings its own tests (`testsuite/tests/tool-expect-test/principal*.ml`) and re-promoted upstream expect files.

notes.title: Combining the two outputs
notes.text: Each run corrects only its own half (`corrected`), and `combine` keeps a `Principal{|...|}` block only when it differs from the default one. This is upstream code (commit 9dc1ddfb2f), cherry-picked as `ba068ca404`.

what.short: The bytecode expect-test tool, a toplevel that runs [%%expect] files.

vox.short: Also accepts the options in Clflags.arg_spec, where the verifier registers its flags, so expect tests can pass -smt-timeout, -dvc and the like.

what.short: The native-code expect-test tool, which also checks [%%expect_asm] blocks.

vox.short: Installs the verifier at startup and accepts its command-line options, like expect.ml.
